examples.japanese: {重力|じゅうりょく}で{物|もの}が{落|お}ちる。
{月|つき}の{重力|じゅうりょく}は{地球|ちきゅう}の{約|やく}6{分|ぶん}の1だ。
examples.english: The Moon's gravity is about one-sixth of Earth's.

examples.japanese: {宇宙|うちゅう}ステーションでは{重力|じゅうりょく}がほとんど{感|かん}じられない。
examples.english: On the space station, gravity is barely felt.

examples.japanese: ニュートンは{落|お}ちるリンゴを{見|み}て{重力|じゅうりょく}の{法則|ほうそく}を{発見|はっけん}したと{言|い}われている。
examples.english: Newton is said to have discovered the law of gravity upon seeing an apple fall.

notes:
The fundamental force that attracts objects toward the center of a massive body such as a planet. In everyday Japanese, used frequently in science education and also figuratively in expressions about being pulled toward something.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {重力|じゅうりょく}が{働|はたら}く: gravity acts/works
- {重力|じゅうりょく}に{逆|さか}らう: defy gravity
- {無|む}{重力|じゅうりょく}: zero gravity, weightlessness
- {重力|じゅうりょく}{加速度|かそくど}: gravitational acceleration

RELATED WORDS:
- {引力|いんりょく}: attractive force, gravitation — a more general term for any pulling force
- {万有引力|ばんゆういんりょく}: universal gravitation (Newton's concept)
- {遠心力|えんしんりょく}: centrifugal force — the outward counterpart
